topic: Treatment of goodwill and revaluation of assets

questions.q: Upon the admission of a new partner, a Revaluation Account is opened. If the revaluation of assets and liabilities results in a net profit, how is this profit treated in the books?
options: It is credited to the new partner's capital account only
It is credited to all partners' (old and new) capital accounts in the new profit-sharing ratio
It is credited to the old partners' capital accounts in their old profit-sharing ratio
It is carried forward to the new Balance Sheet as a Capital Reserve
questions.explain: Profits or losses arising from the revaluation of assets prior to a new partner's admission belong exclusively to the **old partners**, as the changes in asset values occurred during their tenure. Therefore, revaluation profit is **credited to the old partners' capital (or current) accounts using their old profit-sharing ratio**.
